feedback: The plan has the right high-level components (alignment, global structure, local artifacts, VQA only if needed), but it is not specific enough to the class label and the actual visible evidence to approve. For a Hussar monkey, the most discriminative checks should emphasize species-relevant traits visible in the image such as facial patterning, muzzle/cheek hair, overall slender long-limbed build, tail length and attachment, and coat coloration, rather than centering step 1 on lower-body anatomy alone. The structural step still reads partly like a generic checklist instead of being tightly adapted to the likely failure modes here: species confusion with other guenons/monkeys, ambiguous hind-limb versus tail attachments around the branch, and whether the visible face and body proportions support this specific class label.
